summary: Vermilion County, IL: 72-ft observation tower at Forest Glen Preserve, erected 1969, open to climbers; FFLA lists it as a replica, the 2021 magazine does not.

facts.design: Observation tower with cab, about 72 feet tall (the 2021 magazine calls it a fire tower and cab)

access.note: Preserve open to visitors; the 2026 district event invited climbers to the tower. Address 20301 E 900 North Road, Westville.

visit.trail_note: Tower parking lot is east of Pine Knoll Pavilion; a short gravel path leads to the tower, which has 99 steps to the top (district release, 2026).

events.note: Erected in 1969 purely as an observation tower overlooking the Vermilion River Valley, per Amy Steeples (Illinois Country Living, 2021); the magazine says it was never used for fire prevention

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia, the district's 2026 release and the Foundation's property page give 72 feet; the 2021 magazine gives 74 feet. The story and facts use 72 feet (21.9 m).

corrections.why: FFLA lists it under Relocated / Replica Lookouts, but the 2021 magazine says it was erected in 1969 purely as an observation tower and never used for fire prevention. No source read names an earlier lookout that it copies. Editor to decide whether the replica label stays.

sources.title: Vermilion County Conservation District Tower at Twilight Hike, Forest Glen Preserve (district release)

notes_for_editor: The FFLA 'replica' label is not explained by any source read. No earlier fire lookout is named on this site, so the original-site coverage the guide asks for is empty; the story says only what the listing and the magazine say. The Forest Lookouts page for this site (centraluslookouts.weebly.com/forest-glen-forest-preserve.html) is a stub with only the name and county, so it is not cited. Height conflict: 72 ft in four sources, 74 ft in the 2021 magazine; height_m uses 72 ft. Spelling differs across sources (Vermillion on Wikipedia and the Forest Lookouts page, Vermilion elsewhere); the story uses Vermilion. The 2026 district release is a press item reprinted by Vermilion County First; it announces a June 27, 2026 hike in advance, and no source read confirms that the hike took place. No new photos found.
